topic: 口语专项：深入讨论与四项复测 · Independent new scenario: global and local responses to shared problems
grammarFocus: 概括、比较、推测、条件与让步；基于个人错误进行复查。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: Shared Problems, Different Responses: A Simulated Community Case Study
instructions: 项目原创模拟场景与数据，不是官方试卷。阅读文章后独立回答10题，再检查逐题依据。题目包含信息定位、论证范围、比较及推断；遇到词汇可用划词帮助，但使用帮助不算独立测评。语法先看规则，再做新语境练习。
passage:
In the small coastal town of Marlow Bay, a problem that began far away gradually became impossible to ignore. For years, residents had noticed that the tide seemed to bring more plastic than fish. The town council, led by Mayor Elena Ruiz, first responded by organizing monthly beach clean-ups. These were popular, but they did not address the source of the waste. Meanwhile, a group of local fishermen, including Tomás Herrera, reported that their nets were catching fewer fish and more debris. They argued that the problem was not just local; it was regional, because currents carried rubbish from neighboring countries. The council, however, was reluctant to spend money on a problem that seemed to come from elsewhere.

A turning point came when a university research team published a study showing that microplastics had entered the local food chain. The study, led by Dr. Aisha Patel, was not without limitations: it relied on a small sample and had not yet been peer-reviewed. Nevertheless, it prompted the council to act. Mayor Ruiz proposed a pilot project to install floating barriers at the mouth of the bay. The barriers, designed by a local engineering firm, were intended to collect debris before it reached the beaches. Some council members objected, arguing that the barriers would interfere with fishing and might even harm marine life. After a heated debate, the council approved a six-month trial, with funding from a regional environmental grant.

The trial produced mixed results. The barriers did capture a significant amount of plastic, but they also trapped seaweed and small fish. Fishermen complained that the barriers made navigation difficult. Tomás Herrera, who had initially supported the project, now expressed doubts. "We need a solution that works for everyone," he said. "If we only focus on the barriers, we might ignore the root cause." The council decided to modify the design, adding escape hatches for marine life and reflective markers for boats. These changes reduced the bycatch, but the barriers still required frequent maintenance.

At the same time, a grassroots group called Blue Marlow began a campaign to reduce single-use plastics in local businesses. The group, founded by a retired teacher, Clara Nguyen, organized workshops and persuaded several restaurants to switch to biodegradable containers. This effort was smaller in scale than the barrier project, but it had a direct impact on daily habits. Some residents argued that the campaign was too focused on individual responsibility, while corporations continued to produce most of the waste. Clara responded that local action could inspire broader change. "If we wait for global agreements," she said, "we may never start."

The town's experience attracted attention from a regional network of coastal communities. Representatives from three neighboring towns visited Marlow Bay to learn about both the barriers and the plastic-reduction campaign. They noted that Marlow Bay's approach combined technological and social measures, which was unusual. However, they also observed that the town had advantages: a relatively wealthy population, a supportive mayor, and access to grant funding. These conditions might not exist elsewhere. As a result, the visitors concluded that while the barrier project could be adapted, the plastic-reduction campaign might be more transferable, because it required fewer resources.

Back in Marlow Bay, the council commissioned a second study to evaluate the long-term effects of the barriers. This study, conducted by an independent consultancy, found that the barriers had reduced plastic on beaches by about 30 percent, but at a cost of $50,000 per year in maintenance. The report recommended a combination of barriers and upstream measures, such as working with manufacturers to reduce packaging. It also noted that public support was crucial: without community buy-in, even well-designed projects could fail.

The consultants also cautioned against reading the beach figure as a measurement of total marine pollution. Their survey counted visible items on selected beaches; it did not measure all particles in the water or establish what happened farther along the coast. Storms and changes in collection schedules could influence the counts. A neighbouring town was proposed as a comparison site, but it differed in tourist numbers and tidal conditions, so a simple comparison would need careful qualification. The council agreed to report those differences, together with maintenance costs and unintended effects. A policy could be useful without being sufficient, and a positive local result was not a guarantee that another town would obtain the same benefit.

Mayor Ruiz reflected on the lessons. "We started with a local problem, but we learned that it was connected to global patterns," she said. "The barriers were not a silver bullet, but they taught us how to experiment and adapt. The plastic campaign showed us that small actions can add up. In the end, the most important thing was to keep the conversation going." The town now plans to share its findings with the regional network, hoping that other communities can learn from both its successes and its mistakes.

One resident, a shop owner named Mr. Chen, summarized the mood: "We are not heroes. We just tried something, and when it didn't work perfectly, we changed it. That is what a community does."

questions.prompt: What did the town council first do about the plastic problem?
questions.explanation: 原文第一段明确说镇议会最初组织每月海滩清理，因此答案是 Organized monthly beach clean-ups。
questions.evidence: The town council, led by Mayor Elena Ruiz, first responded by organizing monthly beach clean-ups.

questions.prompt: Why did the fishermen see the waste problem as regional rather than purely local?
options: Currents carried rubbish across national boundaries.
The council had stopped all local collection services.
Every local restaurant had already eliminated plastic.
The new barriers were installed in neighbouring countries.
answers: Currents carried rubbish across national boundaries.
questions.explanation: 洋流将邻国垃圾带来，说明废物来源越过当地边界；其他选项没有原文依据。
questions.evidence: They argued that the problem was not just local; it was regional, because currents carried rubbish from neighboring countries.

questions.prompt: What was one limitation of Dr. Patel's study?
options: It used a very large sample
It was funded by the council
questions.explanation: 原文说该研究 had not yet been peer-reviewed，即尚未经过同行评审，因此答案是 It was not peer-reviewed。
questions.evidence: it relied on a small sample and had not yet been peer-reviewed.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was a concern raised by some council members about the barriers?
options: They would cost too much to build
They would interfere with fishing and might harm marine life
They would attract too many tourists
They would not collect any plastic
answers: They would interfere with fishing and might harm marine life
questions.explanation: 原文提到部分议员担心屏障会干扰捕鱼并可能伤害海洋生物，因此答案是 They would interfere with fishing and might harm marine life。
questions.evidence: Some council members objected, arguing that the barriers would interfere with fishing and might even harm marine life.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: The barriers also trapped seaweed and small ______.
questions.explanation: 第三段原文为“they also trapped seaweed and small fish”，因此填fish。
questions.evidence: they also trapped seaweed and small fish.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: The council added escape hatches for marine life and reflective markers for ______.
questions.explanation: 第三段提到“adding escape hatches for marine life and reflective markers for boats”，因此填boats。
questions.evidence: adding escape hatches for marine life and reflective markers for boats.

questions.prompt: Which contrast between the two local responses is supported?
options: The barriers intercepted existing debris, while the campaign tried to change everyday plastic use.
The barriers removed the need for upstream action, while the campaign replaced all regional policies.
The campaign required more grant funding than the engineering project.
Only the barriers depended in any way on public support.
answers: The barriers intercepted existing debris, while the campaign tried to change everyday plastic use.
questions.explanation: 屏障用于拦截已有垃圾（原文：The barriers, designed by a local engineering firm, were intended to collect debris before it reached the beaches.），社区运动则减少企业日常使用的一次性塑料，两者功能互补；原文不支持取消上游行动、运动更昂贵或只有屏障需要公众支持。
questions.evidence: At the same time, a grassroots group called Blue Marlow began a campaign to reduce single-use plastics in local businesses.

questions.prompt: The visitors from neighboring towns concluded that the plastic-reduction campaign might be more transferable because ______.
options: it was led by the mayor
it had already been adopted by corporations
it did not need community support
questions.explanation: 原文明确说明减塑运动可能更便于推广，因为 it required fewer resources，即所需资源更少。
questions.evidence: the plastic-reduction campaign might be more transferable, because it required fewer resources.

questions.prompt: Which statement overgeneralises the reported thirty-percent reduction?
options: All forms of marine pollution throughout the region fell by thirty percent.
Counts of visible items on selected beaches declined.
The costs of maintenance should be reported alongside the benefit.
The local result may require qualification before being transferred.
answers: All forms of marine pollution throughout the region fell by thirty percent.
questions.explanation: 测量对象是选定海滩的可见垃圾，不能推广到全地区所有海洋污染；其他选项符合明确范围、成本和可转移性限制。
questions.evidence: Their survey counted visible items on selected beaches; it did not measure all particles in the water or establish what happened farther along the coast.

questions.prompt: Why would using the neighbouring town as a comparison require caution?
options: Differences in tourism and tides could affect the comparison independently of the policy.
Its measurements were guaranteed to be identical to Marlow Bay's.
It had already demonstrated that all barriers were ineffective.
The consultants regarded comparison sites as always useless.
answers: Differences in tourism and tides could affect the comparison independently of the policy.
questions.explanation: 比较镇的游客量和潮汐不同，可能独立影响垃圾量；这要求限定比较，而不是证明屏障无效或一概拒绝比较。
questions.evidence: A neighbouring town was proposed as a comparison site, but it differed in tourist numbers and tidal conditions, so a simple comparison would need careful qualification.

grammar.title: 概括、比较、推测、条件与让步（Summarizing, Comparing, Speculating, Condition and Concession）
grammar.explanation: 比较要说明比较的对象和维度，如smaller in scale than。while既可表示同时发生，也可表达对比，判断要看两边信息；不能把它一律解释成“虽然”。although +从句与despite +名词/-ing都可表示让步。可能性可用may/might，但不能当成已证实因果。第二条件句可表达与当前事实相反或较不可能的情况，if +过去式，主句would/could +原形；过去反事实则用had +过去分词及would have +过去分词。统计范围限定和程度词要准确，部分有效不等于完全解决。
grammar.example: If we only focus on the barriers, we might ignore the root cause.

questions.prompt: Express a concession: capturing plastic was beneficial, but there was also a harmful effect. ___ the barriers captured plastic, they trapped small fish.
questions.explanation: 题干指定让步，即承认好处但指出坏处；Because改成因果，Unless改成条件，So不能在此引前置从句。
questions.evidence: Express a concession: capturing plastic was beneficial, but there was also a harmful effect. Although the barriers captured plastic, they trapped small fish.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: The campaign was smaller ______ scale than the barrier project.
questions.explanation: 固定搭配 in scale 表示“在规模上”。
questions.evidence: This effort was smaller in scale than the barrier project.

questions.prompt: The town currently lacks enough funding. Imagine the contrary situation: If the town ___ more funding, it could expand the trial.
questions.explanation: 题干明确当前资金不足，设想相反情形用第二条件句if had + could expand；不是预测真实将来收入，因此不能用has或will have。
questions.evidence: The town currently lacks enough funding. Imagine the contrary situation: If the town had more funding, it could expand the trial.

questions.prompt: Report a possibility that has not been proved, without implying obligation or a firm deduction: The new design ___ reduce bycatch.
questions.explanation: may保留尚未证实的可能性；must表示必要性或强推断，has to表示义务，cannot排除可能，都不符合题干。
questions.evidence: Report a possibility that has not been proved, without implying obligation or a firm deduction: The new design may reduce bycatch.

questions.prompt: Choose the best option: ______ the high maintenance cost, the council continued the trial.
questions.explanation: Despite 是介词，后接名词短语；Although 后接从句。此处后接名词短语 the high maintenance cost，故用 Despite。
questions.evidence: Despite the high maintenance cost, the council continued the trial.

questions.prompt: The escape hatches were not installed last year, and extra fish were trapped. Express a contrary-to-fact past possibility: If the hatches had been installed, fewer fish ___.
questions.explanation: 过去反事实结果用might have +过去分词，并且fish是被困住，所以用被动been trapped；其余选项时态、语态或动词形式错误。
questions.evidence: The escape hatches were not installed last year, and extra fish were trapped. Express a contrary-to-fact past possibility: If the hatches had been installed, fewer fish might have been trapped.

questions.prompt: Express a contrast, not a cause: The engineering scheme required substantial funding, ___ the volunteer campaign used fewer resources.
questions.explanation: whereas对比两种方案；because说明原因，so that说明目的/结果，provided that引条件，均改变题干要求的关系。
questions.evidence: Express a contrast, not a cause: The engineering scheme required substantial funding, whereas the volunteer campaign used fewer resources.

questions.prompt: Preserve this condition: Without community support, the project will fail. The project will fail ___ the community supports it.
questions.explanation: unless相当于if not：除非获得支持，否则失败。even if表示有支持也失败，as soon as表示一支持就失败，because把支持变成失败原因。
questions.evidence: Preserve this condition: Without community support, the project will fail. The project will fail unless the community supports it.
